Man Buys New 2017 Dodge Viper GTC for $127,885, Drives 854 Miles, Sells for $242,500
30 photos
Photo: Bring a Trailer
Remember when you could buy a brand-new Dodge Viper in the high five-figure range? Later on it was low six-figures, but regardless, those days are long gone. And if you want a pristine fifth-generation example with a top spec, you'll find yourself spending 2026 Corvette ZR1 money.
Case in point, this 2017 Viper GTC TA 1.0, which just sold for a whopping $242,500 at auction. The seller had previously purchased the car new for $127,885. Not a bad haul for a supercar the likes of which has since gone extinct. The odometer currently shows just 854 miles, which is next to nothing. I'm not sure I'd want to add to it, though. This might be more of a collectible than anything else.
Let's not forget how the fifth-gen Viper was already an endangered species back in 2017. Dodge discontinued production that very same year, so these cars were always going to be collectibles.
Personally, I always thought the final-gen Viper was one of the best-looking American sports cars/supercars ever made. Everything from the proportions to the stance... it's absolutely stunning. Not as stunning as the first-gen model, but stunning nonetheless.
I still can't get over the fact that we live in a world without a modern-day Dodge Viper. Stellantis could definitely use a "win" after this whole Charger Daytona fiasco, and a new-gen Viper would silence a lot of critics - as long as they don't mess it up.
Speaking of not messing things up, this spec right here . Just wow.
The Venom Black exterior with the black Sidewinder II wheels, plus the optional Time Attack 1.0 Package, which makes the car a lot more interesting from a driving enthusiast's standpoint - you've got the revised two-mode Bilstein DampTronic system courtesy of the TA suspension, while other visual and practical highlights include the GTS hood, rear spoiler, tinted windows, HID headlights, side-exit exhaust outlets, Brembo brakes, and Pirelli P Zero Corsa rubber.
The cockpit is as driver-focused as they get, with those power-adjustable Sabelt seats, power-adjustable pedals, carbon fiber accents, Alcantara headliner, an 18-speaker Harman Kardon high-performance sound system, a backup camera, and more. There's a lot of Laguna premium leather here, including on the door panels, instrument panel and even the center console - thanks to the optional Laguna Interior Package.
Photo: Bring a Trailer Last but not least, we've got the Viper's greatest asset , it's magnificent naturally aspirated 8.4-liter V10 engine, good for 640 horsepower and 600 lb-ft of torque. Everything gets sent to the rear wheels via a Tremec six-speed manual transmission and a limited slip differential.
It goes without saying that should the Viper get revived any time soon, there's no way it'll be putting down less than 900 horsepower. And no, I'm not just guessing, because for most of its history, the Dodge Viper was way more powerful than the standard Corvette, and just as powerful as any of the flagship Vette specs.
This fifth-gen Viper GTC packs a similar punch to a C7 Corvette Z06, while older versions were somewhere in the same ballpark as the C6 ZR1. So it stands to reason that a next-gen Viper would try to match the C8 Corvette at the top end of the range. Meaning either the ZR1 or the ZR1X.
